subject: APAC/EU region availability — hosting preference & fallback strategy
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@cloudhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from this morning's call

Hi Emily / Amit,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call highlights:
- Primary constraint: CloudHealth.ai requires EU data residency for any records that contain core PII (customer records, claims history).
- APAC traffic (support workflows in Singapore) can be routed regionally but customer wants the option for APAC-only processing for latency-sensitive workflows.
- Security team will need SOC 2 evidence + network architecture details and the ability to run a brief pen-test in the pilot.

Recommended paths to evaluate (short form):
1) Hosted API (EU region) — fastest onboarding; meets EU residency for processing when we pin to a EU-hosted model. Best for quick PoC but cross-border logs/analytics may need configuration.
2) Dedicated capacity (EU-dedicated) — reserved GPUs in EU, predictable throughput, isolates customers at the infra layer; good middle ground for performance and data control.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — full control for data jurisdiction and network egress, required if legal prohibits any cross-border telemetry.

Actions I propose:
- Security deep-dive scheduled w/ your SecOps + our compliance engineer (30–45 min) — please propose times.
- I'll attach a short SOC2 checklist and our deployment matrix so you can see tradeoffs by option.
- If you prefer, we can scope a 4-week pilot on Dedicated in EU with an APAC routing fallback to Singapore for non-sensitive traffic.

Thanks — attaching the doc set.

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0118
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-checklist.pdf, redwood-deployment-matrix.xlsx
From: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@cloudhealth.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from this morning's call

Thanks, Jonas — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: Any PII for EU residents must remain and be processed within EU boundaries — that rules out cross-border processing for core workflows.
- For APAC: our Singapore support cluster can tolerate outbound calls to a Singapore endpoint for low-latency paths, but billing/analytics data can be routed to central analytics in EU (we can redact PII).
- On Dedicated vs Private VPC: our legal team prefers Private VPC for production if there is any risk of cross-border telemetry. That said, they are open to a Dedicated pilot if we can demonstrate granular control over logging/egress and provide an auditable separation (SLA + contractual clause).

Next asks before we commit to a pilot: 
1) Can you send a network diagram showing where tokenization & KV caches live (we want to confirm no PII leaves the EU region)?
2) Any blockers for a short pen-test during pilot?
3) Ballpark OPEX delta between Hosted (EU pinned) vs Dedicated vs Private VPC for a 4-week pilot (estimate only).

Cc'ing Amit (Infra) who will be involved in the technical checks.

Best,
Emily Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure | CloudHealth.ai
emily.nguyen@cloudhealth.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@cloudhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from this morning's call

Emily — great, thanks for the clarifications. Answers inline and next steps below.

1) Network & dataflow diagram: attached (network-diagram.png). In our Hosted & Dedicated deployments the KV cache and tokenization happen inside the model-serving tier. If we pin to an EU region (hosted or dedicated) all served tokens and KV cache remain in-region. For Private VPC we can place the serving tier in your VPC so nothing leaves your network.

2) Pen-test: allowed during a pilot — we have a standard security-friendly pen-test window and can provide a contact from our Security team to coordinate scope & rules. We will require a short NDA addendum for the exercise.

3) Ballpark delta (per 4-week pilot, very rough):
- Hosted (EU pinned): lowest setup cost; OPEX approx $2.5k–$4k depending on throughput.
- Dedicated (EU reserved small pool): predictable $12k–$18k for the period (includes reserved throughput/headroom).
- Private VPC (customer-managed infra on cloud): higher SOW + onboarding for VPC peering and network ops; estimate $20k+ for initial setup plus your infra run costs.

Suggested next steps to keep momentum:
- Security deep-dive: propose Tue 22 Jun, 10:00–10:45 PT (our Compliance lead + infra architect). Confirm if that works for you and Amit.
- I’ll get Marissa to pull a short pricing sheet and an NDA addendum for the pen-test.
- If you want a low-touch path we can spin up a Hosted EU-pinned PoC in 2 business days; Dedicated pilot typically requires 7–10 business days for capacity allocation and onboarding.

If it helps, we can draft a one-page mutual action plan for the pilot timeline & deliverables.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-diagram.png, redwood-deployment-matrix.xlsx
